title: Embedding-space drift instrumentation and A/B probe for production rerank pipelines
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Background: We have observed small but recurring regressions in reranker quality for several customers when model variants or quantization profiles change. Root causes often point to shifts in the embedding space (drift caused by tokenizer changes, model updates, or quantization noise) that downstream pairwise scoring and calibration layers are sensitive to. Current NDCG/MRR instrumentation exists in several places but lacks fine-grained per-customer promptset hooks, live drift detection, and an automated A/B probe path that can exercise alternative embedding normalization strategies in prod with negligible latency overhead.

Goal: Instrument embedding-space stability and provide an online A/B probe that: 1) tracks per-customer cohort NDCG and MRR with promptset-aware sampling, 2) computes lightweight embedding drift metrics (cosine centroid shift, variance growth, top-k neighbor entropy), 3) exposes a runtime A/B hook to run an alternate embedding normalization / re-scaling path for a configurable fraction of traffic, and 4) surfaces alerts and rollback guidance to Console and the rerank ops runbook.

Scope: This ticket implements the instrumentation + probe wiring only. It includes: (a) ingest adapters for customer promptsets (sampled, privacy-preserving), (b) embedding drift calculators that run as part of the rerank preprocessor and emit time-series to the metrics pipeline, (c) NDCG/MRR per-cohort aggregator that joins model outputs to ground-truth relevancy labels when available, (d) an A/B probe toggle with deterministic bucketing and server-side feature flag that can enable 'normalized-embedding' variant, and (e) dashboards and alert rules in Console. Performance constraints: the probe path must add <=1ms P50 token overhead and must be opt-in per-customer.

Non-goals: Retraining models, changing production ranking objective, or adding heavy-weight offline eval infrastructure (those are separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Aggregated per-customer NDCG and MRR metrics appear in Console for three pilot customers and update within 5 minutes of event arrival.
2) Embedding drift metrics (centroid cosine shift, stdev across embedding dims, top-10 neighbor entropy) emitted as time-series with retention at 90 days.
3) A/B probe flag can be toggled in Console for a customer and deterministically buckets 0%, 1%, 5% traffic to the normalized-embedding variant.
4) Latency overhead measured end-to-end for the probe path is <=1ms P50 and <=5ms P95 on the dedicated serving fleet.
5) Playbook document links to rollback steps and explains alert thresholds for medium/high drift.
6) Unit and integration tests cover drift calculators and bucketing code.

2026-02-28 Alex Moreno: Initial prototype pushed to feature/emb-drift-probe (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1482). Prototype computes centroid shift and per-batch cosine distribution. Microbenchmark: added ~0.9ms P50 on a c6i-like baseline; needs optimization on GPU path.

2026-03-03 Dina Park (QA): Early test uncovered double-counting of sampled promptset events when retry path hits. Adding idempotency token to ingest adapter. Filing follow-up ENG-33211 for retry idempotency across pipelines.

2026-03-06 SRE - Noah Jacobs: Observability note — metrics cardinality could spike if we tag per-prompt. Recommendation: roll up to customer-cohort+model-version granularity and keep raw prompt hashes sampled at 0.1%. Updated metrics plan: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/emb-drift-plan

2026-03-09 Design review (Priya): Confirmed that probe normalization options include (a) L2 re-scaling, (b) layernorm post-quantization, (c) small temperature rescale. We will expose option (a) and (c) for pilot. UX for Console flag approved (mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/emb-probe-console-mock.png)

2026-03-12 Alex Moreno: Merged PR for deterministic bucketing and feature flag backend (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1499). Started integration tests against dedicated fleet. Next: dashboard wiring and alert thresholds; will coordinate with customer success for pilot rollout.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Sampling vs full-cardinality — we chose sampled raw prompt hashes to keep metrics cost low; 2) Lightweight drift signals (centroid & entropy) chosen over full subspace PCA to minimize CPU/GPU impact; 3) Probe runs on preprocessor to avoid re-ranking hot path changes, but that requires careful KV cache compatibility checks.
